chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 102h online + 3h offline (optional) + 1h Final exam + 44h self-study
chung.Description:
This Course includes the specialization "Leading: Human Resource Management and Leadership" and the MOOC "Ethics of Artificial Intelligence".

Leading: Human Resource Management and Leadership specialization is designed to help students become an adaptable leader, ready to face the challenges of the disrupted workplace. This specialization will equip students with the skills to lead and navigate the ever-changing global environment we now work in. Through four themed courses students will: learn how to motivate staff with meaningful work (Become a Meaning Maker); better enable your organization to deliver on its strategic objectives (Know Your Organisation); harness your team’s diversity and use teamwork to innovate and increase your organization’s output (Know Your People), and strengthen your personal leadership skills (Adapt Your Leadership Style).

The MOOC Ethics of AI deals with the ethical issues created, aggravated or transformed by AI. It is intended to give students a chance to reflect on the impact of AI on ethical, social and cultural aspects by focusing on the issues faced by and brought about by professionals in AI and information technologies. The MOOC will address these topics by means of case studies and examples analyzed by using the main ethical frameworks.
chung.StudentTasks: Access the specialization on Coursera and complete all courses' requirements to earn a certificate of completion for the specialization, in order to be qualified for the Final Exam.
chung.Note:
1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

2) Final Exam (FE) = Theoretical Exam (TE)

3) Final Result (FR) = min (10, TE + Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria: TE>=4 and FR>=5

Explain how individuals may differ across a range of attributes including their personality, values, perceptions, and emotions
Explain the motivational characteristics of work and apply these to job design
Analyse the implications of workplace diversity, including challenges and potential benefits
Analyze the role of team dynamics and composition in the team performance
Critically evaluate the similarities and differences between traditional and contemporary theories of leadership
Analyse how post-industrial forms of participative and self-organising leadership might enable or disable effective cross-functional teamwork
Examine the complexities and challenges of day-to-day organisational life might require agile shifts between different leadership styles
Evaluate approaches to influencing and creating meaning at work
Evaluate, create and apply strategies to leverage meaning making through branding
Evaluate and apply approaches to meaning making that play a role in aligning employee buy-in of organisational narratives
Situate discussions of meaning making within broader social contexts and concerns.
Acquire a broad perspective on the ethical impacts and societal implications of AI
